itens.t: Global tech stocks plunge over fears of AI curbs in US
itens.r: Asian markets plunged sharply on Friday, tracking a broad sell-off in Western stocks following the recent US midterm elections. Investors expressed growing anxiety over potential regulatory curbs on artificial intelligence and data center investments in the United States. South Korea's benchmark Kospi index was hit particularly hard, briefly dipping below the 5,000 mark during intraday trading. Analysts note that the market rout reflects profound uncertainty regarding the future pace of tech infrastructure development under a shifting political landscape.
itens.d:
Global tech stocks experienced a sharp plunge on Friday, tracking a significant sell-off in Western markets following the US midterm elections. Investors grew increasingly anxious over potential regulatory curbs targeting artificial intelligence.

The market downturn quickly spread to Asian exchanges, where major indices recorded steep declines as traders reacted to the growing political uncertainty and the looming prospect of tighter rules surrounding technology investments.
itens.e:

itens.t: Kospi plunges 6% amid brutal AI sell-off
itens.r: South Korea's benchmark Kospi index plummeted 6 percent as fears of tighter US regulations on AI rattled markets. The sharp decline sent the index below the 5,000 threshold during intraday trading.
itens.d:
Fears of tighter regulations on artificial intelligence data center investments following the US midterm elections rattled markets. This uncertainty sent South Korea's benchmark Kospi index below the 5,000 mark during intraday trading on Friday.

According to the Korea Exchange, the index ultimately closed at 5,059.69, marking a 6.02 percent decline from the previous session. Earlier in the day, it plunged as low as 4,911.28, triggering a circuit breaker and a sell-sidecar before recovering slightly.
itens.e:

itens.t: Arms review committee approves plan for nuclear-powered submarine project
itens.r: South Korea's state arms review committee passed the basic plan for the country's nuclear-powered submarine program. The decision moves forward efforts to build the strategic naval asset.
itens.d:
A review committee of South Korea's state arms agency passed the basic plan for the nation's nuclear-powered submarine program. The decision-making body under the Defense Acquisition Program Administration approved the Jang Bogo N project during a regular meeting, with a formal launch set for 2027.

Seoul unveiled the initiative in May with the goal of domestically developing and building nuclear-propelled, conventionally armed attack submarines. The first vessel is scheduled to be launched in the mid-30s and fielded after the late 2030s, having been exempted from standard preliminary feasibility studies.
itens.e:

The first vessel is scheduled to be launched in the mid-30s and fielded after the late 2030s, having been exempted from standard preliminary feasibility studies. This strategic advancement matters significantly for national defense capabilities and long-term security planning, directly involving defense contractors, state planners, and regional stakeholders as South Korea pursues indigenous military technological growth.

One factor to monitor is the progression of the project toward its formal launch in 2027. itens.t: North Korea's army of world-class hackers is secret weapon that took down Binance
itens.r: State-backed North Korean hacking units have emerged as a formidable global threat, reportedly orchestrating sophisticated cyber attacks including the takedown of major crypto exchange Binance. Intelligence officials highlight these operations as a key source of revenue for Pyongyang.
itens.d:
North Korea possesses a highly skilled army of world-class hackers that functions as a secret digital weapon. According to reports from Reuters, this specialized cyber force was responsible for taking down the major cryptocurrency platform Binance.

The operation highlights the growing sophistication and strategic threat posed by state-sponsored cyber actors operating from North Korea, targeting global financial infrastructure with significant disruptive capabilities.

itens.t: President nominates arms procurement chief as justice minister
itens.r: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung nominated DAPA chief Lee Yong-cheol as the new justice minister. The post had remained vacant for more than two months.
itens.d:
President Lee Jae Myung nominated Defense Acquisition Program Administration chief Lee Yong-cheol as justice minister, according to an announcement by Cheong Wa Dae on Friday. The post had remained vacant for over two months, with the presidential office citing Lee's strong legal background and administrative experience.

Lee is a lawyer formerly affiliated with Minbyun, an organization known for protecting human rights and promoting democratic values. He previously served as a presidential secretary for civil affairs and legal affairs during the Roh Moo-hyun administration, assisting in anti-corruption reforms.

itens.t: 'We got it done!' Spacewalking astronauts finish installing next-gen ISS solar arrays
itens.r: NASA astronaut Anil Menon and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk successfully completed a grueling spacewalk to finish installing next-generation solar arrays on the International Space Station. The upgrade significantly boosts the orbiting laboratory's power generation capacity.
itens.d:
Two astronauts successfully completed a spacewalk to install and deploy the eighth and final International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array. Expedition 75 flight engineers Anil Menon and Joshua Kutryk worked on the starboard side to augment the station's power systems.

The successful extravehicular activity lasted nearly seven hours and allows the legacy solar array wings to produce up to 30 percent more electricity. Despite encountering a minor issue with the expected shunt current, the crew accomplished their primary installation objectives.

itens.t: NASA announces experimental X-70 Fractal aircraft: A 'new beginning for aeronautics'
itens.r: NASA unveiled concepts for its newest experimental aircraft, the X-70 Fractal. The crewed, rapidly reconfigurable research platform aims to test advanced aviation technologies.
itens.d:
NASA has revealed plans for its experimental X-70 Fractal aircraft, designed as a highly maneuverable test bed featuring rapidly reconfigurable flight-control technology. The modular architecture will allow the agency to swap internal and external components on-the-fly during crewed missions.

According to NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, the aircraft represents a new beginning for aeronautics and is expected to make its first flight within two years. The Fractal is designed to cruise at a speed of Mach 0.75, comparable to a Boeing 737 Classic.

itens.t: China lays out plans to land astronauts on the moon 'before 2030.' Can NASA still win this race?
itens.r: Chinese space officials detailed their roadmap for a crewed lunar landing before 2030 at the 7th Manned Space Symposium. The announcement intensifies the modern space race for lunar return.
itens.d:
China has outlined its roadmap for a crewed lunar landing campaign during the 7th Manned Space Symposium in Beijing. The ambitious plan consists of four distinct missions culminating in a touchdown before the end of 2030, keeping pressure on NASA's Artemis program.

The progression begins in 2027 with the maiden flight of the Long March 10A rocket and cargo resupply mission, followed by uncrewed lander tests, orbital rendezvous rehearsals, and ultimately a dual Long March 10 crewed lunar landing mission.

itens.t: Ads in Chatbots Have Arrived. Here’s What’s Working—and What’s Not
itens.r: AI chatbot developers are increasingly experimenting with advertisements to monetize their platforms. While some companies like Anthropic vow to keep their assistants ad-free, others are testing user receptiveness.
itens.d:
As Anthropic maintains its firm commitment to keeping advertisements out of the Claude chatbot platform, competitors across the artificial intelligence industry are racing to introduce ads.

Companies are attempting to find profitable models by winning over corporate advertisers without generating severe user backlash or disrupting the conversational experience.

itens.r: A UK-backed startup named Potential Sciences is leveraging artificial intelligence models trained on computer-generated biochemical data to accelerate drug discovery. The approach bypasses traditional, time-consuming laboratory testing phases.
itens.d:
Potential Sciences, a startup backed by the UK government, is developing innovative approaches to accelerate the notoriously slow process of discovering new pharmaceutical drugs. 

The company is betting that training advanced artificial intelligence models directly on computer-generated biochemical data can effectively replace traditional and laborious laboratory work.

itens.d:
The startup Aina is developing a wearable smart ring designed to function as a dedicated physical remote control for virtual assistants and autonomous artificial intelligence agents.

The device aims to reduce user reliance on smartphones, allowing individuals to trigger and manage the complex digital actions of their autonomous agents with a simple tap.

The unusual scoring play highlighted the enduring skill of the star guard, who maintained complete control despite the defensive contact. The moment added extra excitement to the matchup between the two players who previously won four NBA titles together.

itens.t: Midwestern City Lights Photographed from the International Space Station

itens.t: Wisconsin infant dies of measles as state sees first death from disease since 1990
itens.r: Health officials in Wisconsin announced the death of an infant due to measles, marking the state's first fatality from the virus in 36 years. The tragic case underscores concerns over declining vaccination rates.
itens.d:
An infant in Wisconsin died of measles, marking the state's first fatalities linked to the disease in 36 years, according to the Department of Health Services. The child, residing in the southwestern part of the state, succumbed to severe complications from the vaccine-preventable illness.

Health officials expressed profound sadness over the tragedy, noting that the state has reported over 400 measles cases across multiple counties during the current outbreak, prompting urgent reminders for the public to verify their vaccination status.

During a rescheduled concert appearance in Los Angeles, the 86-year-old singer shared details of his week-long hospital stay, which included two days in intensive care before doctors cleared him to return to the stage.

itens.t: Eleanor Coppola faz carta de amor à filha em “Making Marie Antoinette”
itens.r: Documentary reflections highlight Sofia Coppola's landmark 2005 film 'Marie Antoinette', the first production granted permission to film inside the Palace of Versailles. The project remains a defining milestone in the director's career.
itens.d:
In 2005, Oscar-winning director Sofia Coppola began filming her ambitious historical biographical film Marie Antoinette, marking the first time a production was permitted to shoot inside the Palace of Versailles.

Among the crew was Eleanor Coppola, the director's mother and a veteran documentarian, who captured intimate, behind-the-scenes footage. Twenty years after the film's release and following Eleanor's passing, those historical recordings have been edited into a new documentary titled Making Marie Antoinette.

itens.t: Enceladus in Silhouette captured in stunning new space imagery
itens.r: Astronomers highlighted new imaging of Saturn's icy moon Enceladus, showcasing its dramatic plumes against the backdrop of space.
itens.d:
A striking space image captured by the Cassini spacecraft showcases Saturn's icy moon Enceladus backlit in silhouette by the sun.

The dramatic illumination highlights the continuous icy plumes erupting from the moon's south pole, which scientists believe connect to a subsurface liquid ocean hidden beneath its frozen shell.

itens.t: Earth has captured a new mini moon — but it won't stick around for long

itens.d:
Earth has temporarily captured a new mini-moon designated 2026 QQ8, which entered planetary orbit earlier this year and will remain under Earth's gravitational pull through December.

Measuring only about six feet in diameter, the small space rock poses no threat to the planet, as its natural orbital path will cause it to break away and depart in 2027.

itens.t: NASA's Voyager 1 probe bounces back from communications glitch in interstellar space

itens.d:
NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft successfully restored communications after a brief 48-hour blackout caused by an onboard glitch in interstellar space.

Engineers determined that the distant probe automatically switched to backup thrusters when its primary system encountered an issue, allowing the mission team to resume normal operations nearly one light-day away from Earth.

itens.t: You don't have to go to the moon to see Earth differently: Artemis II astronaut Victor Glover
